title: Android: Fix gamepad L2/R2 digital button bindings.

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
L2 was previously bound to `MISC1` and R2 bound to `PADDLE1`. This PR instead brings Android gamepad support (for gamepads that lack analog triggers) in line with iOS.

The previous bindings didn't really make a whole heap of sense in general. They were implemented as magic number, I _assume_ they were the result of a manual input off-by-1 error and that they were _meant_ to be bound to `PADDLE1` and `PADDLE2`. I did consider just binding them this way, however doing so is still not likely the behavior that developers or end-users expect. L2 and R2 typically appear as triggers, and your average user probably isn't overly aware there's a distinction between their digital "triggers" (really buttons) and analog triggers found on Xbox/PS controllers. The user will expect these buttons to fire weapons & grenades, accelerate and brake etc. which in Godot _typically_ (obviously bindings come into play here) are handled by `LTRIGGER` and `RTRIGGER`.

As such, now when a digital L2/R2 is pressed the buttons trigger a `LTRIGGER`/`RTRIGGER` axis event of 1.0, and when released trigger an event with 0.0. On iOS, this functionality is built into Apple's GameController framework, on Android we instead implement this behavior in Godot itself.

# Implementation

I've done away with the magic numbers to try mitigate issues like previous L2 => `MISC1` binding. There's no overhead here, `static final int` will be inlined.

I've also fixed another off by 1 bug, the previous implementation had `button = keyCode - KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BUTTON_1 + 20`, where as it should have been `button = keyCode - KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BUTTON_1 + 21`.

Finally, although I haven't really gone out of my way to make this a priority. Rather it's just a benefit of the implementation changes; `button` is no longer blindly mapped/returned. Previously, if this function was called with an unhandled keycode with a value less than `KEYCODE_BUTTON_A`, say `KEYCODE_ALT_LEFT`, then we would have returned a negative button index and probably been in for a bad time. I have no idea if there are gamepads out there that'll do any such thing, but this is now handled nonetheless.

# iOS Reference

Triggers (analog and digital) are handled by [`GCExtendedGamepad`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/gcextendedgamepad). [`leftTrigger`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/gcextendedgamepad/lefttrigger) is a [`GCControllerButtonInput`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/gccontrollerbuttoninput) which extends [`GCControllerElement`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/gccontrollerelement). `GCControllerElement` has an [`isAnalog`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller/gccontrollerelement/isanalog) member that includes the discussion:

> If this property is [true](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Swift/true), the input value defined by the element can return a range (from a minimum to maximum) of possible values. For example, this element might be a pressure-sensitive button or an axis of a thumbstick that allows for a range of physical movement. If this property is [false](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Swift/false), the input value is a discrete value, such as 0 if the element is off, and 1 if the element is on.
